title: XII–XIII. Permission and hardening of fallen angels; names of unclean spirits
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Jude 6). 2 Peter 2:4; but who by means belonging toward free will fell away at ye beginning out from ye truth in that same which they were made, plus became horrible adversaries belonging toward both God plus human beings, plus stand as kept in eternal chains toward judgment (John 8:44; — the reason toward ye naming stands as that same they stand as spirits created by means belonging toward God indeed. 34:14). worthless spirits (1 Kings 16:14), spirits belonging toward error (1 Timothy 4:1), Satan, ye Devil, ye ancient serpent, ye dragon, angels belonging toward Satan (Revelation 12:9), father belonging toward ye lie (John 8:44), spiritual wickedness (Ephesians 6:12), roaring lion (1 Peter 5:8), demons (Luke 11), satyrs (Leviticus 17:7), hairy ones (Isaiah 13:21; — they stand as also called unclean spirits (Luke 11:24). grace denied, stand as made firm in evil — hardening stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which ye fallen. XIII. with divine efficiency suspended, certain angels stand as allowed to fall — permission stands as that same by means belonging toward which. XII.
pass_b_english: XII. Permission is that by which, with divine efficiency suspended, certain angels are allowed to fall. XIII. Hardening is that by which the fallen, grace denied, are made firm in evil.

They are also called unclean spirits (Luke 11:24), worthless spirits (1 Kings 16:14), spirits of error (1 Timothy 4:1), Satan, the Devil, the ancient serpent, the dragon, angels of Satan (Revelation 12:9), father of the lie (John 8:44), spiritual wickedness (Ephesians 6:12), roaring lion (1 Peter 5:8), demons (Luke 11), satyrs (Leviticus 17:7), hairy ones (Isaiah 13:21; 34:14). The reason for the naming is that they are spirits created by God indeed, but who by free will fell away at the beginning from the truth in which they were made, and became horrible adversaries of both God and human beings, and are kept in eternal chains for judgment (John 8:44; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6).
source_text: XII. Permissio est, qua suspensa efficientia divina angeli quidam labi sinuntur. XIII. Obfirmatio est, qua lapsi negata gratia in malo firmantur. Dicuntur etiam Immundi spiritus (Luc. 11:24), spiritus nequam (1 Reg. 16:14), spiritus erroris (1 Tim. 4:1), Satan, Diabolus, serpens antiquus, draco, angeli Satanae (Apoc. 12:9), pater mendacii (Ioh. 8:44), spiritualis nequitia (Eph. 6:12), leo rugiens (1 Pet. 5:8), daemonia (Luc. 11), satyri (Lev. 17:7), pilosi (Es. 13:21; 34:14). Ratio denominationis est quia sunt spiritus a Deo quidem creati, sed qui a veritate in qua conditi erant in principio libera voluntate defecerunt, et horribiles tam Dei quam hominum adversarii facti sunt, et aeternis ad iudicium vinculis servantur (Ioh. 8:44; 2 Pet. 2:4; Iudae 6).
